T1.name: Alex
T1.text: When a bad-parameter hint is very long, the error text can run past the terminal. Please compact the displayed hint in `BadParameter.format_message`: when its visible terminal width is over 20 columns, keep the first 8 and last 8 characters of the hint and join them with `...`; otherwise leave it unchanged. Use the existing terminal-width measurement so ANSI styling does not inflate the count. For example, `param_hint='--abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'` with message `must be positive` should produce `Invalid value for --abcdef...stuvwxyz: must be positive`.

T2.name: Alex
T2.text: Add a new `pretty_output` property on `Result` for readable test failure diffs. It should reflow the captured output as paragraphs through Click's existing text-wrapping helper using the helper's normal defaults, not a hardcoded width. For example, a command that prints `' '.join(['word'] * 16)` on one line should make `pretty_output` break after the first fifteen words, while a short `'hello'` output should stay `'hello'`.

T3.name: Blake
T3.text: When an invocation rejects a flag because someone attached a value to it, I want the returned Result to expose the option spellings involved so tests can assert them without checking the whole error string. For example, with `@click.option('--verbose', is_flag=True)`, invoking `['--verbose=yes']` should make `result.unexpected_flag_values` equal `['--verbose']`; normal successful runs should give `[]`.

T4.name: Casey
T4.text: Add a choice_option decorator in decorators.py that creates an option constrained to a small list of choices and, when no help argument is supplied, auto-generates a help line listing each choice separated by a spaced slash. Example: @click.choice_option('--color', choices=['red', 'blue'], default='red') should register an option whose help text is 'Allowed values: red / blue'; if the caller passes help='Color to use.', keep that help unchanged. Use the option's generated metavar to discover the displayed values rather than maintaining a second hard-coded list.

T5.name: Alex
T5.text: In src/click/termui.py, when _build_prompt renders a Choice type, join the displayed choices with ` | ` instead of the current comma-space separator. Keep the surrounding parentheses and the rest of prompt construction unchanged. This affects the choice list shown by click.prompt, not error messages or metavars.

T6.name: Blake
T6.text: Please add an opt-in `envvar_from_path=True` keyword to `click.option` so an option can read an environment variable whose name is derived from the context’s already-formatted command path, the same string Click uses to show nested commands. For a command `app sync` with `@click.option('--api-key', envvar_from_path=True)`, setting `APP_SYNC_API_KEY=abc` should supply `abc`, while an explicit `--api-key def` should still win. Nested groups should be included so subcommands get naturally scoped env vars.

T7.name: Casey
T7.text: Add a new ExistingPaths parameter type for options that take several filesystem paths at once. It should accept a list or tuple, verify each path exists without opening it, and return the paths; on failure, report all missing paths in one error using Click's usual file-error wording for each one. For example, ['present.txt', 'missing-a.txt', 'missing-b.txt'] should mention missing-a.txt and missing-b.txt together, while ['present.txt'] succeeds.

For a command whose `--level` option has custom shell completion returning `-5` and `-10`, typing `--level -1` and pressing Tab should call that option callback with `-1` and show the numeric completions, not fall back to option-name completion. T2.name: Alex

T3.name: Blake
T3.text: Add a new `Result.short_help` attribute that `CliRunner.invoke()` populates from the invoked command’s normal short help. For a command whose help is `'Print a friendly greeting to the user.'`, `result.short_help` should be exactly that sentence; for clearly longer help text it should use Click’s existing shortening with an ellipsis.

T4.name: Casey
T4.text: Prompt defaults can become visually very wide. Please make the default hint in prompts wrap with Click's existing text-wrapping helper, leaving the helper's library default width in charge rather than adding another width setting, so a long default like 'alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa lambda mu nu xi omicron pi rho sigma tau upsilon phi chi psi omega' renders as a two-line default hint, while a short default like 'ok' stays on one line. Add coverage for both prompt and confirm.

T5.name: Alex
T5.text: In src/click/parser.py, the parser currently appends the same parameter object to the returned order list every time that option appears. Please change it so repeated occurrences are deduplicated: order should keep only the first occurrence of each parameter object, while the parsed option values still update normally.

T6.name: Blake
T6.text: Add an optional `help` argument to `click.prompt` (default `None`). When it is non-empty, print a compact one-line hint above the prompt by reusing the existing short-help summarizer with its normal defaults, rather than inventing new formatting. For example, `click.prompt('Project', help='Process files from the current directory and update the index after each successful batch of changes. The command is safe to rerun.')` should show `Project` and then `(Process files from the current directory...)` before reading the value.

T7.name: Casey
T7.text: Add an optional `help` argument to `click.prompt` that prints explanatory text before the question. Use the existing general text-wrapping behavior with its normal defaults, not a hand-rolled `textwrap` call, so the help block respects the same width as other help text. For example, `click.prompt('Name', help='This note explains the accepted values and is long enough to need a second line')` should show the note wrapped over two lines at the left margin, then the normal `Name: ` prompt; omitting `help` must leave output unchanged.

With total 10 and 4 completed, show `60% left`; with total 8 and 1 completed, show `88% left`.
